Abstract: Spoken solfège consists of reading musical notation aloud by naming each note while preserving its notated rhythm. On the collection with the narrowest corpus range, pitch deviation reaches approximately one quarter of that range, and the generated exercises exhibit a mild one-directional narrowing of the pitch-descriptor profile. Overall, the generated material preserves the reference difficulty profile sufficiently closely to provide candidate exercises for additional same-level sight-reading practice.

Future research should investigate how beginner-level Japanese learners from diverse geographic regions (for example, even within Asia, distinctions can be observed among East Asia, Southeast Asia, West Asia, Central Asia, and North Asia) perceive and utilize the music-generation AI tool “Suno”. Such research would allow for a more comprehensive validation and deeper understanding of how linguistic, cultural, and personal factors mediate the effectiveness of music-generation AI in foreign language education.
